```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
# Write all example files to a temporary folder
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = tempdir())
```

ggsaveR replaces `ggplot2::ggsave()` with a version whose extra behaviour is
switched on with global options. The options are set once, at the top of a
script, and apply to every `ggsave()` call that follows. Existing code does
not need to change.

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(ggsaveR)

p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, wt, colour = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(x = "Fuel economy (mpg)", y = "Weight (1000 lb)", colour = "Cylinders")
```

Without any options, `ggsave()` behaves as in ggplot2. It returns the paths
of the files it wrote, invisibly:

```{r}
ggsave("plain.png", p, width = 5, height = 3.5)
```

## Setting options

`ggsaveR_options()` sets one or more options, checks them, and returns the
previous values so they can be restored:

```{r}
old <- ggsaveR_options(formats = c("png", "pdf"))
getOption("ggsaveR.formats")
options(old)
```

The same options can be set with `options()` by prefixing them with
`ggsaveR.`, for example `options(ggsaveR.formats = c("png", "pdf"))`.
Calling `ggsaveR_options()` without arguments lists the current values.

## Several formats and sizes

The `formats` option turns one `ggsave()` call into several files. The
extension of `filename` is replaced by that of each format.

```{r}
old <- ggsaveR_options(formats = c("png", "pdf"))
print(ggsave("economy.png", p, width = 5, height = 3.5))
options(old)
```

Each format can also have its own size, resolution and other `ggsave()`
arguments. Settings in a format take precedence over arguments given in the
call, and arguments in the call fill in whatever a format leaves out.

```{r}
old <- ggsaveR_options(formats = list(
  list(device = "png", width = 180, height = 120, units = "mm", dpi = 300),
  list(device = "pdf", width = 180, height = 120, units = "mm")
))
print(ggsave("economy.png", p))
options(old)
```

### File names that describe the size

If two formats would write to the same file, such as a PNG for a journal and
a PNG for slides, ggsaveR adds the size to their names:

```{r}
old <- ggsaveR_options(formats = list(
  list(device = "png", width = 85, height = 60, units = "mm", dpi = 600),
  list(device = "png", width = 254, height = 143, units = "mm", dpi = 150)
))
print(ggsave("economy.png", p))
options(old)
```

The size is the one ggplot2 actually uses, after `scale` and default
dimensions are applied. Raster formats also include the resolution. With
`size_suffix = TRUE` every file gets a size suffix; with `FALSE`, clashing
names are an error. A format can also carry its own `suffix`:

```{r}
old <- ggsaveR_options(formats = list(
  list(device = "png", width = 85, height = 60, units = "mm", suffix = "_journal"),
  list(device = "png", width = 254, height = 143, units = "mm", suffix = "_slides")
))
print(ggsave("economy.png", p, dpi = 150))
options(old)
```

## Output folder

`dir` places every file saved with a relative name in one folder, which is
created if needed. Absolute paths are left alone.

```{r}
old <- ggsaveR_options(dir = "figures")
print(ggsave("economy.png", p, width = 5, height = 3.5))
options(old)
```

## Protecting existing files

By default an existing file is overwritten, as in ggplot2. With
`overwrite_action = "unique"`, ggsaveR adds a number instead:

```{r}
old <- ggsaveR_options(overwrite_action = "unique")
ggsave("draft.png", p, width = 5, height = 3.5)
ggsave("draft.png", p, width = 5, height = 3.5)
options(old)
```

With `"stop"`, an existing file is an error. When several files are saved at
once, the check covers all of them before anything is written, and
`"unique"` gives them all the same number so they stay together.

## Bypassing ggsaveR for one call

`guard = TRUE` hands the call unchanged to `ggplot2::ggsave()`, whatever
options are set:

```{r}
old <- ggsaveR_options(formats = c("png", "pdf"))
ggsave("only-png.png", p, width = 5, height = 3.5, guard = TRUE)
options(old)
```

Scripts that use `guard` need ggsaveR to be loaded; `ggplot2::ggsave()`
does not know the argument.

## Masking

ggsaveR attaches ggplot2 when it is loaded, so its `ggsave()` takes
precedence whichever package is loaded first. `ggplot2::ggsave()` always
reaches the original.
